title: Grace Period, Automatic Premium Loan and Nonforfeiture Provision of Whole Life Insurance
content:
## Provision

**Grace.** When an installment of an Ashgrove Whole Life Insurance policy is unpaid on its due date, the policy enters the grace period, which lasts the tier's grace period in calendar days, or the number of days the tier sets for the issue state where the issue state has its own grace period. Coverage continues during grace.

**Time limit for cure.** The overdue premium must be received no later than the last day of grace, which is the unpaid installment's due date plus the grace period days. The last day of grace is found by adding the grace period length in calendar days to the due date; payment received on that day is in time. The due date is the paid-to date the policy record shows (the due date of the next unpaid installment), and the length follows the policy's issue state.

**Automatic premium loan.** If the grace period ends unpaid and the owner has elected the automatic premium loan on a tier where it is available, an automatic premium loan pays the overdue installment on the last day of grace, provided the loan value available under the policy loan provision covers it; the policy then returns to in force.

**Nonforfeiture.** Otherwise the nonforfeiture provision applies as of the unpaid installment's due date: the owner's elected option, or the tier's default option when none was elected.

- Extended term insurance continues the base face plus the paid-up additions face, less indebtedness, for the period the net cash value buys. It is not available, and reduced paid-up applies instead, where the tier does not offer extended term to rated classes and the underwriting class is table rated or a tobacco class.
- Reduced paid-up insurance is bought by the net cash value at the net single premium per 1,000 of paid-up insurance. Where it would buy less than the tier's smallest reduced paid-up face, the net cash value is paid in cash and the policy is surrendered.
- Any loan is extinguished against the cash value when a nonforfeiture option applies.
- With no net cash value the policy lapses.

Within the tier's election period after the unpaid installment's due date, the owner may replace the default with the other option or with cash surrender, effective as of the same due date. Extended term coverage ends on its expiry date; it has no loan value and pays no dividends.

**Values.** The net cash value is the guaranteed cash value plus the paid-up additions cash value plus the dividend accumulations, less the loan balance. The reduced paid-up face is the net cash value divided by the net single premium per 1,000, multiplied by 1,000, rounded to the whole dollar.

## Boundary cases on the last day of grace (hypothetical, grace period of 31 days)

| Unpaid installment due | Last day of grace | Payment received | In time |
|---|---|---|---|
| March 1 | April 1 | April 1 | Yes |
| March 1 | April 1 | April 2 | No |
| January 31 | March 3 (in a year where February has 28 days) | March 3 | Yes |

On a policy issued in a state with a 60-day grace period, an installment due March 1 has its last day of grace on April 30.

## Worked values (hypothetical)

Guaranteed cash value 18000.00, paid-up additions cash value 2500.00, dividend accumulations 1200.00, loan balance 4700.00: the net cash value is 17000.00. At a net single premium of 425.00 per 1,000, it buys 17000.00 divided by 425.00, multiplied by 1,000, that is 40000 dollars of reduced paid-up face.
